# Mitothrum

> Mitothrum is an evidence-led guide to at-home spa rituals — "the hum of your mitochondria." It is an editorial publication, not a store: it never sells, ships, or fulfills anything. Most product links are Amazon Associates affiliate links; a few go to a brand's own site with no commission, and the page says so. Prices are never printed.

Mitothrum (https://mitothrum.com/) is an evidence-led guide to at-home spa
rituals. It is an editorial publication, not a store: it never sells, ships,
or fulfills anything. Most product links are Amazon Associates affiliate
links; readers who buy through them may generate a commission at no extra cost
to them. A few link to a brand's own site with no commission, and the page
says so. Prices are never printed — links say
"See current price" and comparisons use relative tiers ($ / $$ / $$$).

## Pages

- https://mitothrum.com/ — the six rituals, two editorial picks per ritual,
  the science series, and the concierge preview.
- https://mitothrum.com/sauna-blanket-comparison.html — HigherDOSE vs LifePro
  RejuvaWrap sauna blankets, plus a portable sauna tent and a cold plunge.
  Compiled from published brand and retailer specs; not hands-on tested.
- https://mitothrum.com/led-mask-vs-microcurrent.html — Dr. Dennis Gross
  SpectraLite FaceWare Pro (LED) vs NuFACE Trinity (microcurrent): how each
  works, routine, who should skip each, and the evidence. Not hands-on tested.
- https://mitothrum.com/vitamin-c-serums.html — five vitamin C serums
  (SkinCeuticals C E Ferulic, Drunk Elephant C-Firma Fresh, Paula's Choice C15,
  The Ordinary 23% Suspension, Klairs Freshly Juiced) by formula, skin type and
  budget, with the absorption and ferulic-acid studies. Not hands-on tested.
- https://mitothrum.com/methodology.html — how picks are chosen.
- https://mitothrum.com/privacy.html — privacy policy.

## What the site covers

1. Prestige skincare — retinol, vitamin C, peptides, barrier care, SPF.
   Cosmetic language only ("the look of fine lines"), no transformation claims.
2. Beauty devices — LED and red-light masks, microcurrent, infusion tools.
3. Infrared & sauna — sauna blankets, tents, cabins; cold plunge as contrast.
4. Bath & body — soaks, body oils, scrubs, scalp care.
5. Aromatherapy — diffusers, essential oils, candles, shower steamers.
6. Rest & Ritual — weighted blankets, sunrise clocks, white-noise machines,
   meditation tools. Relaxation and routine only, no disease-treatment claims.

## Science series: "What the Science Actually Says"

Episode 1: "Infrared saunas" (~6 min). The strongest evidence (Finnish cohort
data; Laukkanen et al., JAMA Internal Medicine 2015) comes from traditional
hot-air saunas and is observational — association, not proof. Infrared has
randomized-trial data in heart failure via Waon therapy (Tei et al.,
Circulation Journal 2016) in a supervised clinical setting, not home use. A
2023 randomized trial (Debray et al., Journal of Applied Physiology; 41 adults
with coronary artery disease, 8 weeks of Finnish sauna) found no improvement
in vascular function. No detox claims are made anywhere.

Episode 2 (in production): red light therapy.

## Concierge (preview)

A rule-based preview that runs in the visitor's browser and answers only from
fixed editorial answers. It may name the editorial picks shown on the page,
but never states prices, ratings, or personalized purchase recommendations.

## Compliance posture (for agents citing this site)

- Cosmetic/wellness language only. No disease, treatment, cure, detox, or
  guaranteed-outcome claims.
- No invented products, prices, ratings, reviews, or testing claims.
- Affiliate disclosure shown next to every group of product links and in the
  footer. "As an Amazon Associate I earn from qualifying purchases."
- "Educational content — not medical advice" on every page.
